title: Asleep on a cushion (Mark 4:35–41)
hook: the storm, the cushion, and the question: who is this?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a farmer slept while the earth bore fruit automate, of itself. Your line was it grows while you sleep.

Evening on the Sea of Galilee. After a long day of teaching from the boat, Jesus says: let's go across to the other side. They push off, and the lake does what it's known for: wind comes down off the hills and whips it up in minutes. Waves break over the side; the boat is filling. Several of these men are fishermen who know this lake, and they're terrified. And Jesus? In the back, asleep. Mark gives one detail nobody else does: his head is on a cushion.
screen: `LET'S GO ACROSS.` → `THE BOAT IS FILLING.` → `HE'S ASLEEP.`

segments.voice: In the King James Bible: "he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?" Don't you care? That's the real question in a storm. Not just, will we make it? But, does anyone care? Jesus gets up and speaks to the weather the way you'd speak to a barking dog. "Peace, be still." "And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm." A great storm, then a great calm. Then to them: "Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?" The strange part: now they're even more afraid. Mark says they feared exceedingly, and asked each other, "What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?" Anyone raised on the Psalms knew who commands the sea. In Israel's scriptures, it's God who stills the storm and quiets the waves. That's the question this whole part of Mark keeps asking: who is this? Christians hear the story in two directions. It's about who Jesus is. And it's about storms of every kind: a diagnosis, a debt, a 3am panic. Many take comfort that the disciples' honest cry, don't you care, is right there in scripture, and that the answer came. That closes a week: a family that thought he was mad, a wider family, the sower from a boat, why parables, a lamp on a stand, a seed growing in the dark, and a man asleep on a cushion in a storm.
screen: `CAREST THOU NOT THAT WE PERISH?` · `PEACE, BE STILL.` · `WHY ARE YE SO FEARFUL?` · `WHAT MANNER OF MAN IS THIS?`

segments.voice: Breathe out longer than you breathe in, and let the thing that's been filling your boat lately come to mind; name it plainly. Picture it as wind and waves around a small boat, with the cushion in the back. If you pray, say the old words from the story, peace, be still, and hand the storm over; if you don't, let each out-breath loosen your grip a little.
Cushion, the detail only Mark kept: Jesus asleep in the back of the boat, his head on a cushion, before the storm and the calm.
Your line: why are you afraid? A great storm, then a great calm. Twenty-five weeks now.

howItsDone: Many Christians pray with this story in times of fear, and peace, be still is a line often said or sung in worship and prayed at bedsides and in hospitals.

original.note: Greek: something for the head, a cushion. Its only use in the New Testament is here.

chat.says: In the storm, the disciples wake Jesus and say 'carest thou not?' What happens next?
options: He calms the sea, asks why they're afraid, and they wonder who this is.
He scolds them for waking him and goes back to sleep on the cushion.
He tells them to row harder, and together they make it through the waves.
